363604.title: Conjecture on regularity bounds for squarefree powers of simplicial trees
363604.literal_statement:
Let $\Delta$ be a simplicial tree of dimension $t-1$, let $I(\Delta)$ denote its facet ideal in the polynomial ring $R$, and let $\nu_1(\Delta)$ and $\nu(\Delta)$ denote its induced matching number and matching number, respectively. The squarefree power $I(\Delta)^{[k]}$ is defined for $1\leq k\leq \nu(\Delta)$. **Regularity conjecture.**

$$
k-1+(t-1)\nu_1(\Delta) \leq \operatorname{reg}\left(\frac{R}{I(\Delta)^{[k]}} \right)\leq k-1+(t-1)\nu(\Delta)
$$

for all $1\leq k\leq \nu(\Delta)$. This would extend the expected regularity bounds for squarefree powers of edge ideals to simplicial trees; the preceding proposition establishes the lower bound, while the upper bound is the conjectural part.

363648.title: The dominated-or-dominating pair degree-sum conjecture for supereulerian digraphs
363648.literal_statement:
Let $D$ be a strong digraph with $n$ vertices. A pair is **dominated or dominating** when it is a pair of dominated or dominating nonadjacent vertices of $D$ as specified in the source. A digraph is **supereulerian** if it contains a closed ditrail spanning all vertices, equivalently, a spanning eulerian subdigraph. **The dominated-or-dominating pair degree-sum conjecture.** If for any pair of dominated or dominating nonadjacent vertices $\{u,v\}$ of $D$, 

$$
d(u)+d(v)\geq 2n-3,
$$

then $D$ is supereulerian. This is presented as a possible generalization of the known degree-sum theorem for all nonadjacent pairs, and its resolution is not given in the supplied text.

363660.literal_statement:
Consider a family of matrices to which the Laplace expansion process described in the source is applied. **Convergence conjecture.** For matrix families satisfying specified criteria, the Laplace expansion process always converges.

The source verifies convergence for all examined uniformly banded families, while families with finitely many banding exceptions may require manual manipulations. It leaves both the precise criteria and convergence for non-uniformly banded families open.

364458.title: Borel almost finiteness conjecture for uniformly Borel amenable Følner graphs
364458.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a bounded-degree Borel graph. Call $G$ a **uniformly Borel amenable Følner graph** when it has the uniform Borel amenability and Følner properties defined in the source. Call $G$ **Borel almost finite** if, for every $\varepsilon>0$, there is $k>0$ such that $G$ admits an $(\varepsilon,k)$-Følner tiling.

**Borel Almost Finiteness Conjecture.** Every uniformly Borel amenable Følner graph is Borel almost finite.

This conjecture is a guiding principle for uniformly Borel amenable Følner graphs and was originally proposed by Marks for free amenable actions. Its converse is false: there are Borel almost finite graphs that are not Borel amenable.

364727.title: Sharpness conjecture for forbidden induced subgraphs and JEP decidability
364727.literal_statement: Let $H$ be a graph, let $S$ be a finite set of graphs, and write $\operatorname{Forb}_\subseteq(S)$ for the graphs containing no member of $S$ as an induced subgraph. **One-forbidden-graph sharpness conjecture.** Problem JEP is decidable for all finite sets $S$ containing $H$ if and only if $H\subseteq P_4$. The paper proves the if direction; moreover, $H\subseteq P_4$ is equivalent to $\operatorname{Forb}_\subseteq(H)$ being well-quasi-ordered under induced subgraph containment. The converse direction remains conjectural.

364735.title: Conjecture on products of 2-wise uniform distributions
364735.literal_statement: Let $H$ be a group, let $t$ be a positive integer, and let $X,Y$ be independent random variables that are **2-wise uniform** over $H^{t}$, meaning that every pair of coordinates of each variable is uniformly distributed over $H^{2}$. **Product conjecture.** The product $XY$ cannot have a fixed value; equivalently, $XY$ is not supported on a single element of $H^{t}$. The question is posed in the context of understanding how products of partially uniform distributions increase independence, and the source does not provide a resolution.

364895.title: The common-zero independence-number conjecture for finite groups
364895.literal_statement: Let $G$ be a finite group. The **common-zero graph** $\Gamma_v(G)$ has the non-linear irreducible characters of $G$ as vertices, with two characters adjacent when they have a common zero, meaning that both vanish at some element of $G$. **Common-zero independence-number conjecture.** For any four non-linear irreducible characters of $G$, two have a common zero; if $G$ is solvable, then for any three non-linear irreducible characters of $G$, two have a common zero. Equivalently, the independence number of $\Gamma_v(G)$ is at most three for arbitrary groups and at most two for solvable groups. This is presented as a weaker form of the three-class vanishing conjecture and is not resolved in the supplied text.

365230.title: Submodularity characterization of resistance nonnegativity
365230.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with vertex set $V$, let $c$ be normalized edge weights, and let $\mathcal{S}(G)\subseteq[0,1]^{2^V}$ be the space of resistance capacities. A set function on $2^V$ is **submodular** if it satisfies

$$
f(A)+f(B)\geq f(A\cup B)+f(A\cap B)
$$

for all $A,B\subseteq V$. **Submodularity conjecture.** If $\tau_\bullet(c)$ is submodular, then $p(c)\geq0$. Equivalently, $G$ is RN if and only if $\mathcal{S}(G)$ intersects the submodular cone in $[0,1]^{2^V}$. The forward implication is known from the theorem stated immediately before the conjecture, while the converse is presented as open; a partial result gives $p(c)\geq-1$ under a related submodularity condition.

365283.title: The monotone total positivity conjecture for the Eulerian matrix
365283.literal_statement:
Let $A(n,k)$ be the Eulerian number, and let $A=(A(n+1,k))_{n,k\in\mathbb{N}}$ be the Eulerian matrix. For $i,j,r\in\mathbb{N}$, take the submatrix whose rows are indexed by $i,i+1,\ldots,i+r$ and whose columns are indexed by $j,j+1,\ldots,j+r$.

**Monotone total positivity conjecture.** For all $i,j,r\in\mathbb{N}$, the determinant of this submatrix is a monotonically increasing function of $i\in\mathbb{N}$.

This is proposed as a stronger form of total positivity for the Eulerian matrix. The supplied text gives no resolution, so the assertion remains open.

365343.title: Bang-Jensen and Wang's conjecture on branchings in semicomplete split digraphs
365343.literal_statement:
Let $D$ be a **semicomplete split digraph**, meaning a split digraph whose relevant semicomplete structure has no pair of non-adjacent vertices. It is **$2$-arc-strong** if deleting any one arc leaves a strong digraph. A **good $(u,v)$-pair** is a pair of arc-disjoint out-branching and in-branching rooted at $u$ and $v$, respectively.

**Bang-Jensen and Wang's conjecture.** Every $2$-arc-strong semicomplete split digraph $D$ contains a good $(u,v)$-pair for every choice of vertices $u,v$ in $D$.

This conjecture narrows the general branching problem to semicomplete split digraphs. The source describes related counterexamples for general $2$-arc-strong split digraphs but gives no resolution of this semicomplete case.

365736.title: Baumgart's conjecture that every graphic matroid is SIBO
365736.literal_statement:
A rank-$r$ matroid is **subsequence-interchangeably base orderable (SIBO)** if every pair of bases $A$ and $B$ admits orderings $a_1,\ldots,a_r$ of $A$ and $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ of $B$ such that

$$
(B\setminus\{b_i,\ldots,b_j\})\cup\{a_i,\ldots,a_j\}
$$

is a basis for every $1\le i\le j\le r$. **Baumgart's conjecture.** Every graphic matroid is SIBO. If true, this would imply the proximity conjecture for graphic matroids; the conjecture is presented as open in the paper.

365839.title: Equality of the Helly and Radon numbers for connected graphs under $\Delta$-convexity
365839.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a non-trivial connected graph. Write $h_\Delta(G)$ for its Helly number and $r_\Delta(G)$ for its Radon number with respect to $\Delta$-convexity.

**Helly–Radon equality conjecture.**

$$
h_\Delta(G)=r_\Delta(G).
$$

The conjecture proposes that, unlike in most familiar convexities on discrete structures, the Helly and Radon numbers coincide for every non-trivial connected graph under $\Delta$-convexity. The equality is established in the paper for chordal graphs, and the authors report it for all small graphs examined, but it remains open in general.

365953.title: The Rado triple conjecture for homogeneous quadratic equations
365953.literal_statement:
Let $a,b,c\in\mathbb{N}$. An equation is **partition regular** if every finite coloring of $\mathbb{N}$ admits a monochromatic solution. A triple $(a,b,c)$ is a **Rado triple** in the sense used for homogeneous quadratic equations.

**Rado triple conjecture.** The equation

$$
ax^2+by^2=cz^2
$$

is partition regular if and only if $(a,b,c)$ is a Rado triple.

The necessity follows from Rado's theorem together with the implication that partition regularity of $P(x^2,y^2,z^2)=0$ implies partition regularity of $P(x,y,z)=0$. No instance of a Rado triple is currently known for which the required partition regularity has been proved; notable test cases include $x^2+y^2=z^2$, $x^2+2y^2=z^2$, and $x^2+y^2=2z^2$.

366394.title: Bipartite maximizer and clique free-energy conjectures for the antiferromagnetic Ising model
366394.literal_statement:
Let $G$ range over $\Delta$-regular graphs, let $\alpha_G(B,\lambda)$ be the occupancy fraction, and let $F_G(B,\lambda)$ be the free energy density. **Bipartite maximizer and clique free-energy conjectures.** For all $\Delta\geq 3$ and all $(B,\lambda)\in[0,1]^2$:

1. The complete bipartite graph $K_{\Delta,\Delta}$ maximizes $\alpha_G(B,\lambda)$ over $\Delta$-regular graphs.
2. The complete graph $K_{\Delta+1}$ minimizes $F_G(B,\lambda)$ over $\Delta$-regular graphs.

The first assertion extends the proved $3$-regular result for $K_{3,3}$, while the second concerns free-energy minimization despite the failure of clique occupancy minimization throughout the full parameter space. The supplied text does not state whether either assertion has been resolved.

366730.literal_statement: Let $g\geq 1$ and $\ell\geq 1$, and let $g\mathsf{exc}_\ell$ and $g\mathsf{den}_\ell$ denote the $g$-gap $\ell$-level excedance number and $g$-gap $\ell$-level Denert statistic, respectively. 357195.title: Extended Knuth conjecture for joint arc-count distributions in random digraph depth-first search
357195.literal_statement:
Consider a random multidigraph on $n$ vertices in which the outdegree of each vertex is independently distributed as $\operatorname{Ge}(1-p)$, with $p\in(0,1)$, and endpoints of outgoing arcs chosen independently and uniformly from the $n$ vertices. In a Depth-First Search, let $L,F,B,C,T$ denote the counts of the corresponding arc types used in the paper. **Extended Knuth conjecture.** For every $n\geqslant1$ and every $p\in(0,1)$,

$$
(L,F,B+C,T)\overset{\mathrm{d}}{=}(L,B,F+C,T).
$$

This strengthens Knuth's equality in distribution by asserting a joint symmetry involving the other arc counts. It is presented as a conjecture and no resolution is supplied in the source.

357241.title: Janson's joint distribution conjecture for DFS arc counts
357241.literal_statement:
Consider a random multidigraph on $n$ vertices with geometric outdegree distribution: independently for each vertex $v$, let $d^+(v)$ be geometrically distributed with mode $0$ and mean $\frac{p}{1-p}$, for $p\in(0,1)$, and choose the heads of its arcs independently and uniformly from the vertices. In a depth-first search, let $L,F,B,C,T$ denote the numbers of loops, forward, back, cross, and tree arcs, respectively. **Janson's conjecture.** The random vectors

$$
(L,F,B+C,T)\quad\text{and}\quad(L,B,F+C,T)
$$

have the same distribution.

This extends Knuth's conjecture by asserting a joint distributional symmetry among all five DFS arc types. The source presents it as a proposed extension; no resolution is supplied here.

357404.title: Nice-group conjecture for the cross-index of products of free simplicial posets
357404.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a **nice group**, meaning a cyclic $p$-group or a generalized quaternion group whose order is a power of $2$. Let $\mathcal{P}_1$ and $\mathcal{P}_2$ be finite free $G$-simplicial posets, and let $\operatorname{x-ind}$ denote the cross-index used in the source. **Nice-group cross-index conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{x-ind}(\mathcal{P}_1\times\mathcal{P}_2)=\min\{\operatorname{x-ind}\mathcal{P}_1,\operatorname{x-ind}\mathcal{P}_2\}.
$$
 The authors present this as their strongest open conjecture; their main theorem shows that the analogous assertion cannot hold for arbitrary finite groups.
